groups.checked_argument: All slices are normalized fixed envelopes; common smooth curvature bounds and decreasing compactness prevent the cutoff limit from becoming identically minus infinity. Order sandwiches make the cutoff limit fixed.

The constant left part has initial potential Gamma_a. Taking tau=a gives the lower bound phi+at and all tau<c give phi+ct; ordinary fixedness follows from the internal ordinary-preserves-ideal result.
For beta>=theta every old slice is admissible. Projection gives fixed normalized representatives, preserves order and left constancy.
The weighted scaling and addition formulas use backgrounds (1-s)beta and s beta; their sum is beta. They preserve concavity of projected curves.
Projection preserves all real-weight ideals. Both composed and direct projected slices are fixed in the final background; equal projected curves force the original fixed slices to have equal ideals.
All Hermitian-indexed components share the same ideals by comparing them with eta+eta-prime, which dominates both. The canonical E map is injective.
Compatibility at h/j and h/(j+1) gives q_j>=q_{j+1}, supremum zero and one smooth curvature majorant. Distributional positivity passes to theta in the decreasing L1 limit.
The original normalized limit is a competitor for its own envelope. Growth of admissible envelope families with the background gives q<=P_theta[q]_I<=q_j, and infimum proves equality.
Every positive Hermitian eta dominates h/j for large j. The limit is the pointwise infimum over all eta, so it is independent of the reference h.

R E Gamma is between the fixed original slice and each of its projections. Their equal ideals sandwich the middle ideals; fixed representatives in theta identify R E with identity. E R is below the original system.
Monotonicity with R E=id and E R<=id gives E(Gamma)<=system iff Gamma<=R(system), and hence the greatest realized subsystem assertion.

Equality of the limiting slice ideals to the component ideals is exactly the condition E R=original system. The local modification characterization concerns all local Lelong numbers, not only divisors on X.
Small multiples of a fixed Kahler form lie below every Hermitian form. The extension from Kahler-indexed families is independent of the smaller form by passing to a common smaller Kahler multiple.

Subtracting f changes theta to theta+ddc f. Projection preserves all ideals and curve properties; uniqueness of fixed representatives proves inverse and cocycle. Commutation with E follows in the common final background.
The min/max f inequalities are independent of eta, so limiting slices have the same ordinary type. Their ideals and fixedness prove commutation with R.

The internal smooth torus example uses two positive nonclosed backgrounds differing by ddc f with unequal integrals of their squares. Zero fixed slices have unit ideals before and after the gauge. Their perturbation limits give those different integrals.

The commuting deck transformations define a proper P1 bundle over the elliptic curve. v=w-Im z is invariant off the infinity section, and the written frame norm extends smoothly and positively at the section.
Independent symbolic differentiation checks the three complement Hessian entries and the t(1-tr)/(4(1+tr)) Schur complement. The lower curvature bound gives nefness as t decreases to zero.
Independent differentiation in xi=1/w gives the divisor matrix with off-diagonal i/2 and vertical 1/t. A>t/4 gives positivity also at D; sigma0=pi sigma therefore gives the specified Kahler form.

The lifted psh difference u-psi_D has logarithmic upper growth and the two deck periodicities. The internal periodic subharmonic lemma applied first in z and then w makes it constant; canonical qpsh equality extends across D.

A smooth nef approximation is available for each Hermitian eta. The fixed projections of psi_F+f_eta have only the fiber ideals at every positive real weight and form constant test curves with the prescribed cutoff.

Generic Lelong upper semicontinuity gives at least coefficient one on F in the decreasing limit. Divisorial removal leaves a positive theta current, forced by rigidity to [D]. Hence q=psi_F+psi_D+C and the two transverse poles have the stated floor-rounded ideals.

groups.checked_argument: The new D pole violates the recovery criterion. R E=id makes the original and its different realized subsystem have the same R image, proving noninjectivity of R and nonsurjectivity of E.

Analytic ordinary equivalence makes the residual potential bounded. Closed perturbations epsilon*kappa permit Stokes and expansion of (theta+epsilon*kappa)^2; the trivial normal bundle gives D^2=0. The limiting current [F]+[D] vanishes off its pluripolar support, so its nonpluripolar measure is zero. This does not remove the positive lower-volume and bounded-mass hypotheses in the later recovery theorem.
